title: Vilasa 14. Ramachandra and Govinda Kaviraja; the Festival at Kheturi
html:
Srinivasa at Srikhanda with Raghunandana; Ramachandra Kaviraja comes to Yajigrama, debates with Vyasa and Srinivasa and receives initiation; the healing and initiation of Govinda Kaviraja at Budhari, a song of Govindadasa; Narottama comes to Budhari; the installation of Gauranga and Vallavikanta and the great festival at Kheturi; Narottama's ecstasy; Ramachandra stays with Narottama; the conversion of the brahmins Harirama and Ramakrishna

1Glory, glory to Sri Krishna Chaitanya, the abode of virtues!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, the life of the Vaishnavas!

2Glory, glory to Advaita Acharya and [all] the beloved [of the Lord],
whose appearance is for the deliverance of living beings!

3Glory, glory to Sri Jahnava, the life of Virachandra,
whose manifestation of prema is renowned in story!

4Now I shall write how [Srinivasa] went to Khanda;
I saw what love arose in whom.

5Leaving his conveyance at the gate of the Thakura's house,
he came on foot, bringing his people with him.

6Arriving, he bowed down to Gauranga, [keeping him] on his right;1
at that very time Raghunandana came.

7"Come, come, my brother, my life, Srinivasa!
No one could in any way comprehend your appearance."

8They embraced in love and sat down on their seats,
and Raghunandana, smiling, asks:

9"I have heard everything through people coming and going;
it gives me joy to hear it — so tell me:

10how you went to Vrindavana and what happened there,
how, on arriving, you took shelter at the Prabhu's feet,

11how you studied the books with Sri Jiva,
how the command came: 'Take the books and go.'"

12How he had brought the books by the road through Jharikhanda,
he told him all of it, [and] how many people were with him;

13in what way the theft took place, how it happened,
in what way [the books] were recovered in the king's house.

14I sit listening at Raghunandana's left;
[he told] how he showed mercy to the king, settling in his town,2

15how for that reason the king came to love him greatly,
and how he had recently come to see his mother.

16"For our happiness, stay at Yajigrama;
it is a great joy to me that you live in this place."

17[Raghunandana] spoke of all the household matters:
how he spends his time and on what he relies.

18Sri Sarakara Thakura has passed from sight;3
in that grief Raghunandana is always weeping:

19"This is my great sorrow, this is what lies on my heart:
the Thakura has gone away, leaving his servant behind."

20A spear stayed lodged in the depths of his heart and did not come out;
with arms around each other's necks the two began to weep.

21Weeping, Srinivasa says: "By his mercy
the command came from his holy lips that I should go to Vrindavana;

22and when I came back he was no longer to be seen — such is my lot!"
In separation the hearts of both were overwhelmed.

23That night he stayed there, absorbed in the joy of talk of Krishna;
he stayed there that day, and [another] night came to its end.4

24In the morning they sat in the Sri Nata-mandira;5
Sri Raghunandana says: "What shall I say to you?

25You are my life, brother! The whole burden is yours;
to spend my time with you — that is my wish."

26At the parting they embraced each other;
holding hands, the two set out.

27One day they spent sitting together, the two of them;
[each] thinks within himself that he is still in that place.6

28Raghunandana's form enchants the worlds,
and Srinivasa's form beside it is most beautiful;

29seeing them, my heart was enchanted;
he knows whose eyes the form of the two has caught.

30In this way he came to his own home
and, arriving, bowed down at his mother's feet.

31At this time Ramachandra was in that village;
hearing it from people's lips, he goes quickly to see [the Thakura].

32He goes along the road, thinking in his mind:
"When I see him, how shall I address him?"

33Arriving, he saw the Thakura sitting on his seat;
he is alone, no one else is in that place.

34Arriving, he stands before him and says nothing;
he bows down and gazes at his form with his eyes.

35Placing five coins before him, he bowed down again;
[the Thakura] blessed him and asked him once:

36"Where have you come from?
What is your name, in what village do you live?"

37"My name is Ramachandra, I was born in the Ambashtha clan;
my one desire is to see the Prabhu's feet.

38My birthplace is the village of Teliya Budhari."
There was a seat, and [the Thakura] tells him to sit on it.

39He showed him great honour: "Bathe and eat,"
and gave him a lodging so that he could stay nearby.7

40The next day the Thakura says to him:
"How far from Kheturi is your home?"

41He says: "Four kroshas, I humbly submit."
"How many days ago did you leave home and come?"

42He says: "Four days I was on the road;
on the fifth day I beheld [your] feet."

43"Tell me, have you studied any learning?"
"I have looked into many books and shastras."

44Little by little he questioned him, and he told everything;
hearing him, the Thakura [noted] the skill of his speech.

45Seeing this he is pleased, but does not enter into discussion [of learning];
one day the Thakura bids the Acharya:8

46"Hold a discussion with Ramachandra,
and I shall sit and listen to the waves of your debate."

47Vyasa and Ramachandra, coming together,
joyfully discuss learning.

48First the talk was of grammar and the commentaries,
then the two raised the waves of poetics.

49Long goes the debate, the Thakura sits and listens;
after that a quarrel broke out between the two.

50Seeing that Ramachandra is very strong in logic,
the Thakura himself says to Vyasacharya…9

51The Acharya was struck dumb; the Thakura sits and listens;
calling Ramachandra, he himself embraced him.

52In Ramachandra's heart there is pride:
"Who [can] debate with me in the science of logic?"

53The Thakura himself understood his thought;
stopping the Acharya, the Thakura says something [himself].

54A great debate takes place with the Thakura;
hearing that debate, the Acharya was spellbound.

55The Thakura recognized Ramachandra's ability
and says wondrous words to Vyasa:

56"What sort of pandita he is cannot be grasped;
some divine learning — Sarasvati herself is his helper.

57Such practice, such reasoning, such quickness of mind —
I have not seen anyone who has the like."

58The next day the Thakura holds a debate with Ramachandra;
all that they say, Vyasa listens to.

59Their debate went on until evening;
neither was aware of the outer world, so that not even the bath was taken.

60Then the Thakura broke off and rose:
"Go, Ramachandra, take your bath now."

61From that day he shows him great regard;
one who prizes virtues knows virtues — others do not know them.

62From that day the Thakura loves him dearly;
seeing the radiance of his body, the Thakura is greatly pleased.

63He seats him close by and himself eats [with him];
he knew that Ramachandra was a jewel among men.

64On another day the Thakura sat with him:
"Today you yourself debate with me."

65"As you command," he said, with pride in his heart:
"To converse with the Thakura — that is [a joy] for me."10

66For a whole prahara there was much debate;
[then] the Thakura again says to Ramachandra:

67"Bearing a human body, [a person] acquires a host of qualities;
whatever goal he pursues, that arises in his mind.

68Ignorance and knowledge — whatever he cultivates within —
good qualities and bad all show themselves in the body.

69High and low — all that is achieved through the body,
what ought and ought not to be done, all that has a cause and has none —

70he who, bearing a body, expounds the eternal and the non-eternal
is blessed on earth; but who knows this?

71The shastra by studying which the disease of worldly existence is destroyed —
giving up everything, that is what I long for.

72Otherwise all is in vain — the shastras forbid it;
there are such words in all the shastras, there is no doubt of it.

73Merely studying logic and nyaya, time wastes away;
what gain is there at the end, what do the shastras say [of it]?

74First of all one should ponder the Bhagavata in one's heart;
listen, my son, to what came of that.

75The Bhagavata sets forth the doctrine in every detail;
in it are the words that are the command of Ishvara."

76"That is what I shall do, that is what I shall study, from which there is gain;11
why do other work while time wastes away?

77For this, Thakura, I have come to you:
become the lord of Ramachandra — let all people know it.

78For all my reading and hearing, the doubt in my mind has not gone;
what then am I to do — that is what rises in my mind, mahashaya.

79My life has gone in vain eating lye and oil-cake;12
I gave no thought to my own good and ill.

80In Gauda and in Vrindavana your name is Acharya Srinivasa;
accept Ramachandra, make him your own servant.

81Having become a servant, I hope for these two feet;
only then will the fulfilment of my desire bear fruit.

82Seeing that I am low and fallen, do not spurn me with contempt:
for my deliverance there are your feet.

83If there is delay, time wastes away;
place on my head, Prabhu, your feet that grant fearlessness."

84Weeping, he gazes at his face and rolls on the ground:
"Be my Prabhu birth after birth, without fail!

85I am sold to your feet — take me [as one bought] for a price;
bear in the world the name 'the lord of Ramachandra.'"

86Then the Thakura showed mercy and placed his hand on his head:
"Birth after birth you are mine" — by this he showed mercy.

87Bowing down, he drank the charanamrita;13
mercifully [the Thakura] let him hear the Hari-nama.

88The next day he mercifully gave him the Radha-Krishna mantra
and told him all about the goal, the means and the substance;

89he gave him the method of remembrance14 — the essence of the limbs of sadhana;
he taught him everything and explained its meaning.

90By [the Thakura's] mercy he reads the books of Sri Rupa;
he reads the plays and the Sandarbhas, the commentaries and lexicons.

91Reading, at the merest hint he works out the construction;
how many objections he raises, how much he expounds!

92Such meanings does the Thakura reveal that [Ramachandra] weeps profusely;
embracing him, [the Thakura] calls him the companion of his life.

93Within one month he sat and read through everything;
the Thakura listens while he swiftly sets out the meaning.

94There is no doubt of this, listen, mahashaya:
when the heart is free of offence, everything reveals itself.

95One whose person has such learning and such virtues —
what man would call him ordinary?

96The mood of a former perfection stays attached to him;
at the mere taking of shelter all virtues come and arise.15

97Such are all the doings of the mahantas of old;
he alone understands it who has reached the summit of bhajana.

98Born in the house of a worldly man, [one] seeks another shelter;
shelter with a great soul confers all virtues.

99So too a devotee of Krishna: one on whom is Krishna's mercy,
in his heart there arises [the longing for] shelter at the feet [of the guru].16

100There are words about this in earlier books, and so I write;
if I did not write, the mind would not be attentive.

101Such is Ramachandra Kaviraja, full of virtues:
as the guru, so the disciple — the foremost.

102One day the Thakura is sitting in his own house,
Ramachandra [standing] humbly some way off.

103At that time a letter came from home,
written by Govinda Kaviraja in his own hand:

104"My health is poor — come quickly;
you can stay two or four days and go back again."

105Ramachandra paid no heed and stays with the Prabhu:
he has no leisure, he is ever expounding the books.

106He has no [thought of] food, he is always in sadhana and bhajana;
what he does, where he is, he does not know.

107For another month and a half he stays with the Prabhu;
the time passes ceaselessly in waves of prema.

108Meanwhile Govinda's illness grew worse;
he writes to his elder brother: "Help me!

109My body will not last, the disease is strong —
unless the Prabhu mercifully grants me [his] feet."

110He wrote to him to bring the Thakura:
"I will tell him everything when I see him before my eyes.

111My hands and feet have swollen, grahani has set in."17
He set out everything — what more should he write?

112Having read the letter, the Kaviraja did not tell the Prabhu;
when the Thakura asked, he spoke of something else.

113Now I shall write of the cause of Govinda's illness:
from the grahani disease he is about to give up his life.

114He was a worshipper of the Devi, the shakti Mahamaya;18
by that service, that remembrance, he longs for her mercy.

115He had perfected the mantra, and his deity had appeared to him in person;
at the hour of death he falls prostrate at her feet:

116"In life and in death, Mother, I know no one else;
give me a boat to cross [the ocean of] existence.

117So the time has passed — at the end give me liberation;
who but you will show mercy to Govinda?"

118In anguish he cries out: "Save me!
In life and in death I have no one but you."

119Many people stand around, but there was no vision;
a divine voice spoke — he hears it with his own ears:

120"For deliverance remember Govinda, my son!
You have seen it in the shastras, you have read it, great ascetic.

121Remember Govinda, the giver of deliverance:
He is the maker of heaven, earth and the netherworld.

122Can I bestow the abode of liberation?
I myself meditate on His reddish feet.

123Can I tell His glory?
Maidservants like me He has in such numbers!

124The complete Brahman, the Eternal, the son of Nanda —
hundreds of Durgas like me pray to Him.

125Aja, Bhava19 and the rest find no limit to Him;
hundreds of thousands such serve His feet.

126The Radha-Krishna mantra is the essence of all mantras;
take shelter at those lotus feet.

127The giver of liberation to all is the supreme Govinda;
he who does not worship such a Lord is dull-witted and wicked.

128Remember Govinda, the giver of deliverance:
He is the maker of heaven, earth and the netherworld."

129Hearing her words, his life [all but] fled:
"Where has Ramachandra gone? I do not see him with my eyes!"

130Sending someone who was nearby,
telling of the illness, they called and brought [his guru].

131The guru came; he was given a fine seat;
seating him close by, [Govinda] makes his plea to him:

132"Have mercy, master, let me be delivered!
My ears are stopped, I no longer see with my eyes."

133The guru says: "Remember Govinda in your heart;
who else is there in the world to deliver you?"

134He lies with head bowed, saying nothing to anyone;
[then] he called his own son Divyasimha:20

135"I have spent my life sunk in false delights;
who is there who could deliver me?

136To where Acharya Thakura is staying
quickly send five men, writing a petition.

137Write: my life is in danger, [I beg] the Prabhu to come;
I live only to see him once with my eyes."

138He wrote a letter to Ramachandra Kaviraja
and sent five men with money for expenses.

139They travelled night and day; [with] two dandas of daylight [left],21
within four dandas they reached Yajigrama.

140They asked people: "Where is the Thakura's house?"
"Where there is a big tree to the right of the gate."

141Coming up and seeing the tree at the gate, they halted;22
a man went and gave word to the Kaviraja.

142Hearing, he came out and sees five men;
all of them, handing over the letter, are grieving.

143Having read the letter, he went to the Thakura;
reading the letter to him, he makes a plea:

144"Accept my family, Prabhu;
what should I, a worthless wretch, say in your presence?"

145At his words compassion arose in the Prabhu;
that very day, after eating, he set out.

146The next day they travelled on but could not arrive;
stopping at one place, they spent that night there.

147In the morning they all set out; a man went ahead
and, arriving, said: "The Thakura is coming."

148Govinda Kaviraja Thakura lies [ill];
calling his son, he speaks in great joy;

149in the middle of the village he had banana trees planted
and mango leaves hung all around.23

150Divyasimha went out to meet the Prabhu and brought him;
he bowed down, and then [the Prabhu] asked about him.

151The Prabhu asked, and Ramachandra submits:
"This is Govinda's son — he is your servant."

152He leads the Prabhu to his own house;
with joy in their hearts they cry out "Hari, Hari!"

153Arriving, they stopped at the Kaviraja's dwelling;
the Prabhu says: "What shall I do, Ramachandra Dasa?"

154Ramachandra says: "What shall I say, Prabhu?
Do as you wish — you are independent."

155The Prabhu says: "Your people are my servants,"
and with these words he entered Govinda's house.

156Kettledrums sound, auspicious cries of ulu-ulu ring out;
he went to the room where Govinda lies.

157Two or four men, holding him up, sat him up;
there are no words in his mouth; with his eyes he gazes at [the Prabhu's] face.

158He joins his palms before his face, but words will not come;
the Thakura placed his feet on his head.

159In the house they seated the Prabhu on a fine seat,
anointed him with sandal and other oils, and bathed him.

160He ate some fried dishes and sweets;
Ramachandra took the charanamrita and the remnants from his lips24

161and had Govinda eat them;
the moment he ate, all his illness went away.

162Many provisions came, the cooking was set going;
when the cooking was done, [the Thakura] bathed and cleansed himself.

163The offering is ready and was offered to Krishna;
the Thakura himself sat down and ate.

164Govinda ate the remnants from the Prabhu's plate;
such joy arose in him that he no longer thinks of his illness.

165That night passed, and morning came;
smiling, the Prabhu says to Ramachandra:

166"Bathe Govinda — you have my consent;
I shall bathe and then perform his initiation."25

167Ramachandra bathed him with his own hands,
took off his wet cloth and dressed him in a dry one.

168Having bathed, the Prabhu goes to show him mercy;
who can tell what joy there was?

169Ramachandra sits holding him on his own lap;
the Prabhu gave the "Hare Krishna" mantra into his ear.

170All around, the Vaishnavas sing the sankirtana of the Name;
at this time he has him hear the Krishna mantra.

171Then he mercifully gave the mantra of Radhika-jiu
and explained the meditations on the two separately.

172[Govinda] bowed down, [the Prabhu] placed his feet on his head;
he felt within himself strength like a lion's.

173He offered many gifts — gold, so many cloths,
bronze vessels, brass vessels and more, by the hundreds.

174By the Prabhu's mercy the disorder of the belly26 went away;
he walks about slowly, and his joy is boundless.

175What I write is just as it was, not otherwise;
let no one feel grief on hearing this account.

176Hear the Kaviraja's former words;
what will come later, all shall see:27

177*"The god is not lustful, the goddess is not wanton —
it is only the manifestation of prema.
A servant at the feet of Gauri and Shankara,
says Govindadasa."28*

178By the Prabhu's mercy all [his] virtues came to light;
he who savours [his verses] knows their essence.

179From that day Govinda was well
and comes to the Prabhu in perfect contentment.

180He tells the Prabhu of his former ways;
weeping and weeping, Govinda Dasa begs for shelter:

181"The lamp of our family is my brother Ramachandra;
through my tie with him the Prabhu has shown me mercy.

182How much shall I tell of my own faults?
I am an untouchable wretch, wicked by nature."

183Weeping and weeping, he falls at Ramachandra's feet:
"One whose Prabhu is Srinivasa — what has he to fear?29

184Now I make my plea — hear, best of masters;
I am afraid to speak it — my heart trembles."

185Pada:30

*Worship, O mind, the son of Sri Nanda,
His lotus feet that grant fearlessness.
A rare human birth, the company of sadhus —
cross over this ocean of existence.*

*Cold and heat, wind and rain,
days and nights without sleep —
in vain I served the miserly and the wicked
for a fleeting crumb of happiness.*

*This wealth, this youth, sons and household —
is there anything in them to trust?
Like water on a lotus leaf life trembles —
worship the feet of Hari always.*

*Hearing, chanting, remembering, praising,
serving the feet, the service of a servant,
worship, [friendship,] self-surrender —
this is the longing of Govindadasa.*

186"Now I know: [your] feet are my life;
give the command to describe the lila of Krishna.

187In my mind is the desire to describe the lila of Gauranga,
the describing of which is the highest of all perfections."

188The Prabhu says: "Listen to what I say about what you ask:
describe the lila of Krishna with joy in your heart.

189Vasudeva Ghosha Mahashaya, dear to Gaura,31
has described the very essence of all his virtues;

190you describe freely the lila of Radha and Krishna" —
immersed in bliss, he gave this command.

191"Read, Govinda Dasa, the Rasamrita-sindhu,
by touching a single drop of which one gains blessing everywhere;

192read the Ujjvala,32 where the lila of Radha and Krishna is:
in it is given the whole range of lilas with every rasa."

193At an auspicious moment he began to read the book;
[the Thakura] explained the whole division of its subject-matter.

194As soon as he heard the outline of the book,
he grasped it inwardly and brought out many meanings:

195"I have understood it all — rasa, doctrine, bhava and states;
fulfil this plea of mine.

196I have understood in my mind that this is your mercy;
without Gaura's mercy the lila has no end to be found."

197Smiling, the Prabhu said "Good, good!" and embraced him;
everyone knew that he had realized Gauranga.

198From the time he took shelter at the Prabhu's feet
until his death — what was there not!

199How much sadhana he performed, how much he described!
In this way he spent thirty-six years.33

200From that day he began composing [songs on] the lilas;
he described the lila of Gaura and the lila of Krishna.

201Thus I have told of the virtues of Govinda Kaviraja,
by hearing of which unbelief and ignorance are dispelled.

202I am quite blind, I have not a particle [of understanding];
whatever I write, [I write] by the command of mercy.

203I write by the mercy of these two Prabhus —
by the command of Sri Jahnava and Prabhu Virachandra.

204Listen, listen, hearers, with minds intent;
holding a straw between my teeth,34 I make this plea.

205I write the account of the virtues of Sri Thakura Mahashaya:35
first of all he arranged the service of Gauranga.

206Hearing that the Thakura had come to the Kaviraja's house,
he was plunged at heart into an ocean of bliss.

207He prepared a new temple and all the provisions;
the wish [to hold] a great festival grew strong.

208All his kin, the landholders of the village,
all who carried out his orders — all were enchanted.

209Whatever provisions were wanted, all were ready:
was it [the power of] the guru's command, or the strength of sadhana?

210With two or four men he came to Budhari;
people who went ahead told the Thakura.

211The Thakura rejoiced at his coming —
it seemed in his mind as if he had found life.

212Telling of his virtues, he instructed everyone
to show him honour as before and to greet him [fittingly].

213To Ramachandra Kaviraja and Vyasa Acharya [he says]:
"Quickly, quickly go out to meet him and bring him."

214"As you command," said the two and went out;
not far off, quite near, they saw him.

215Meeting him, the two prostrate themselves;
[he asks:] "Who are you, mahashayas? Tell me."

216Greeting them, he raised them and embraced them,
and came to where the Thakura is sitting.

217On the left Ramachandra, on the right Vyasa;
his body blossomed with delight.

218Seeing him from afar, the Thakura rises to meet him:
"Come, come! [My] life has come and entered my heart!"

219He prostrated himself, [the Thakura] embraced him;
sitting on their seats, they converse.

220He asked after his welfare; [he replied:] "By your command [all is] well;
sorrow has gone because you have come."36

221Govinda Kaviraja came and fell at his feet;
[Narottama] raised him and embraced him tightly.

222"Who is this?" he asked, delighted;
the Thakura says: "This is Ramachandra's younger brother, Govinda."

223There was great happiness at meeting after many days;
Ramachandra invited [them] to bathe.

224Having bathed and drunk water, rapt in talk of Krishna,
they sit on their seats and tell everything in order:

225Acharya Thakura and Thakura Mahashaya —
what their happiness was in Vrindavana, how they came to know each other,

226how on the road the books were stolen;
everyone sits and listens to the sweetness of their words.

227Rapt in talk of Krishna they all spend day and night;
so the night passed, and morning came.

228[Narottama] raised the matter: "Come to Kheturi;
if you do not come yourself, all the joy will be spoiled.

229I know of the command the Prabhu has given:
there is a command to inform you."37

230[Srinivasa:] "You yourself do what you are engaged in;
within five days I shall come without fail."

231[Narottama:] "I cannot stay; I shall go quickly to my village;
only let there be no offence — my life remains [with you].

232Let Vyasacharya come with me — that is my request:
he will surely arrange everything."

233Saying this, he took his leave and went to his own village;
Vyasa had the command: "Go and arrange everything."

234He arrived in the village; his heart was full of bustle;
sending men out, he brings goods from the farthest places.

235Bringing stone, he has an image made manifest in the house:
he summons craftsmen to make Gauranga manifest.

236Many new dwellings were built;
at that time Acharya Thakura set out.

237The Prabhu with Ramachandra came quite near;
Thakura Mahashaya and Vyasa go to bring him in.

238Thakura [Mahashaya] brought him into the house in great joy;
he alone knows [that joy] — who [else] can know?

239How much shall I write of how he was attended?
His house, his goods — what more shall I say?

240The manifestation of the image of Gaura-raya and, with it, one more:
the Acharya took the vow [for the installation], and many with him.

241Men were sent with letters inviting
the mahanta-adhikaris in every village.

242Everywhere invitations were sent to the Vaishnavas:
all were to come on the day of Phalguna Purnima.38

243Thousands upon thousands of people make the arrangements;
thus all are staying with joy in their hearts.

244The Thakura is absorbed in remembrance, sankirtana goes on;
at that time the splendid manifestation of Gaura-raya took place.

245In joy all cry out "Hari, Hari!"
What shall I say of that matchless beauty of form?

246Then came the manifestation of Vallavikanta;39
in everyone's heart there was supreme delight.

247Little by little everyone came and gathered;
in this way the mahanta-adhikaris arrived.

248How many lodgings were set up within the village,
how many near the house, how many in other villages!

249How many new houses, how many awnings —
he knows who saw it; who else knows?

250How many provisions — curd, flattened rice, bananas,
sweets, ukhra40 and sugar!

251Whatever goods were needed were all brought in;41
they brought a hundred jars filled with panchamrita.42

252The Acharya himself performs the bathing abhisheka;
he carried out many rites according to the rules.

253All the mahantas together touched the bodies [of the images]
and put sandal paste and tulasi garlands on them.

254Kirtanas began everywhere, in many places;
who is dancing, singing, rolling on the ground, where!

255When the kirtana began before Gauranga,
no one stayed seated — everyone went there.

256Householders and ascetics, the low and those of low conduct —
all came, no one stayed at home.

257Devidasa Mahashaya began the kirtana;
what singing and playing it was could not be grasped.

258Gaurangavallabha Raya plays the mridanga;
hearing it, one loses all composure, [as if] life itself goes out.

259Gaura-raya is seated, Vallavikanta on his left;
as the sight [of them], so the singing.

260How many mahanta-adhikaris — hundreds!
The Vaishnavas listen to the singing, maddened.

261What sweet singing, what playing!
Hearing it with his ears, who could keep his composure?

262With Acharya Prabhu are Sri Vyasacharya
and Ramachandra Kaviraja: they cannot contain themselves.

263The Thakura dances and sings in such a way
that, unable to contain himself, he falls to the ground, weeping and weeping.

264Tears flow from his eyes in hundreds of streams;
he cannot dance, he has become like a Baul.

265No one can hold back [in him] the transformations of bhava;
seeing them, the hearts of others are amazed.

266Thakura Mahashaya, seeing and hearing, is almost stunned:
what kind of prema this is cannot be understood.

267As he listens, he laughs aloud in happiness;
tears pour from his eyes — how unchecked!

268His composure left him, and he dances in the kirtana;
seeing his trembling and leaping, ten men hold him.

269How his lips tremble — his teeth seem about to fall out!
Pressing his hand to his breast, again and again he falls to the earth.

270His whole body [bristles] as if with the thorns of the shimul;43
now his body swells, now it grows thin.

271Such is the beauty of his body — the transformations of bhava;
the moon of bhava rose in everyone's body.

272Krishnananda Majumdar, with all his people,
falls to the ground, weeping and weeping:

273"When will there again be such a state, such happiness?"
Rolling on the ground, he weeps, clasping everyone's feet.

274Again and again he looks into Narottama's face
and, weeping and weeping, falls down, clasping his feet:

275"You have sanctified [me], my son, together with all my people;
who, born on this earth, has seen such happiness?

276My house has known happiness equal to Vrindavana;
all my people are Narottama's servants."

277Such prema did Narottama reveal in [his] land;
he dances and speaks44 in the delight of prema.

278When everyone began to give [gifts] to the kirtana,
he brings out from the house and gives whatever comes to hand.

279Thakura Mahashaya notices none of this;
what shall I say of [his] prema, how describe it?

280To say nothing of dancing — as soon as he stood up,
everyone thought to himself: his form is just like Gauranga's.

281Whomever he turns and looks at in the rapture of prema,
all those people fall weeping at his feet.

282Acharya Thakura, weeping, embraced him
and, holding him by both arms, speaks very softly:

283"Embodiment of prema, you have filled the world with prema;
seeing it, the heart rejoices and the eyes reach their fulfilment.

284Who has the power to hold such a festival?
All Gaura's mercy is upon you with all your clan.

285Gauranga has consented to be under your sway;
in life and in death no one has any [other] claim."45

286The kirtana ended; they ate and drank;
all go off, each to his own lodging.

287The next day, as the festival was drawing to a close,
all go together to the lodging place.

288A disciple of Thakura Mahashaya named Gokula Dasa
sang in the kirtana that day.

289Beginning, he strikes up the sound of the mridanga;
all hear with their ears [a sound] surpassing nectar.

290Everyone went to the circle of the kirtana;
leaving off the alapa,46 all sing as they go.

291First he sings — how sweetly! — of Gauranga's virtues;
as they listen, it touches everyone to the heart.

292Thakura Mahashaya listens, overcome with bliss;
after that, at the end, he sings of Krishna's lila.

293Pada (in the fitting raga):

*Filling the cupped hands of her eyes,
holding that face before her,
her soul longs to drink.
What has touched her eyes, that she drinks ever;
again and again Radha remembers.*

294As soon as Thakura Mahashaya heard this with his ears,
he embraced him and fell to the ground.

295"Gokula, what you have made me hear — you have robbed me of all peace!"
Saying this, [he weeps:] streams flow down his face and breast.

296Holding the kirtaniya by the hand, he whirls and wanders about;
"What have you made me hear!" he says, crying "Alas, alas!"

297"What perfection — Krishna's form, Radha's love!
She drinks with her eyes — such is her mind."

298In the state of that bhava his heart and mind were immersed;
however much prema there can be, it doubles.

299So, in dancing, the second prahara passed;
by the force of bhava his body was racked.

300Hundreds and hundreds of times he flings himself on the ground;
who has the strength to hold him back?

301What transformation of the heart it is cannot be grasped;
crying "Radha, Radha!"47 he keeps rushing off.

302How his body trembles, where he falls!
Seeing it, [it seems] life will not stay in the body.

303Mother, father, kinsfolk — all weep;
they hold Narottama — his life is in turmoil.

304Seeing this, Acharya Thakura grew anxious at heart;
sitting down, he held him, and he trembles all over.

305He recites a verse from the Ujjvala — Sri Rupa's description —
by which [even] Sri Radha-ramana regains composure.

306Again and again he recites the verse, but [Narottama] does not come to himself;
he devised a remedy: "Take him to another place."

307They took him into the house and laid him down; after a prahara
he came to himself; the bhava changed, and he sat up as before.

308That night all sat rapt in talk of Krishna;
someone raises objections, [another answers] in detail.

309The next day they send off each according to his station;
how much shall I tell of the leave-takings?

310Each was sent off as was fitting;
well pleased, they all go home together.

311Thakura Mahashaya cannot bear the separation;
Acharya Thakura understood his mind.

312He seats Thakura Mahashaya beside him on one seat;
[there is] conversation on Krishna's lila and Krishna's virtues.

313[With them are] Ramachandra Kaviraja and Sri Vyasa Acharya;
Acharya Thakura speaks, and all listen calmly.

314"Come, Ramachandra, speak — let us hear it from your lips;
let the night pass thus in joy and happiness."

315For four dandas Ramachandra tells of Krishna's lila;
everyone's heart rejoices, all forget themselves.

316Ramachandra says: "Listen, Thakura Mahashaya:
there is a wish to hear [it] from your own lips."

317"As you command," said the Thakura and began to speak;
as soon as they hear, no one's heart keeps its composure.

318His mind is overflowing with bhava, he is unaware of the outer world;
how many explanations he gives, how many ornaments of speech in them!

319After this Acharya Thakura joyfully
began to tell of the state of Krishna's purva-raga:48

320what came before and after, how [the feeling] arises and subsides;
he tells it again and expounds it again and again at length.

321All float in bliss, finding no footing;
that night they spent with their bodies blossoming.

322For a month the Thakura stayed, rapt in talk of Krishna;
the happiness of even one day — what shall I say of it?

323One day a certain plan arose in his mind;
the Thakura says to Thakura Mahashaya:

324"There have come to be three homes — I shall speak of it in detail —
in three lands: Kheturi, Yajigrama and Vishnupura.

325There is no way out — so much rises in my mind!
I wish to tell how everything everywhere can be arranged:

326[here] the shelter of Gauranga, [there] my mother's love,
[and] in Vishnupura the king's new bhakti.

327I shall go [there] once and come back again;
[but my] life is near you: this is the essence of the truth."

328Hearing this, Thakura [Mahashaya] was deeply distressed;
"Cruel is the Creator!" he cries, weeping profusely.

329Two or four days passed — he does not say a word;
[Srinivasa says:] "Ramachandra, you stay, hold fast to virtue.

330The two of you — in talk of Krishna's lila, in discussion of bhajana;
stay with him, do not break the command."

331[Ramachandra:] "Whatever command the Prabhu has given, that prevails;
I stay together [with him] — that is my own wish too."

332Hearing these words, Thakura Mahashaya [resolved] in his heart:
"Whether we stay or go anywhere, we two will be together."

333That day, at the parting, Thakura [Mahashaya] was in great grief;
he gave [Srinivasa] for the road two mohurs and two lengths of cloth,

334to Vyasacharya five coins and a length of cloth,
and to the bearers and porters he gave [gifts] all together.

335All the sorrow the two felt then —
that sorrow only he knows whose soul is burning.

336My hard heart could not see it:
so much love, so much prema — and my heart did not melt.

337Such a sight, such a festival, such transformations of bhava —
[and I,] hearing and writing, [remain] with a heart like wood.

338Ramachandra Kaviraja and Thakura Mahashaya
sleep, eat and bathe in one place.

339Ceaselessly they tell of Krishna's lila and ponder it;
they do not notice day or night — such is their love.

340One day, to bathe in the Padmavati,
they go hand in hand with joy in their hearts.

341In the water they splash at each other in mock battle and speak of Krishna;
at that time there came two brahmins, worthy men:

342Harirama and Ramakrishna, sober panditas;
seeing the two, they composed their minds.

343The two went into the water to bathe;
one raises an objection, [the other] sets out the doctrine in detail.

344The two brahmins, learned in the shastras, say nothing;
all the doctrine the others set forth they understand in substance.

345As they listened, the brahmins took up the discussion;
all that they said [the others] refuted with the arguments of the doctrine.

346The brahmins speak words contrary to the doctrine;
all that they say [the others] refute.

347[The brahmins] lay weight on varnashrama, as written in the smriti;
[the others] refute it all with the words of the Bhagavata Purana.

348The two brahmins grow angry, [the others] show forbearance;
again they recite verses — and [the brahmins] stand there struck dumb.

349Having bathed, the two mahashayas came home;
the two brahmins came with them and went inside.

350The Mahashaya, who takes the essence, full of virtue,
offered them seats, and the brahmins sat down.

351Giving them lodging, he had them fed excellent food;
in the evening they saw the Thakura's arati.49

352Seeing the extraordinary image, they rejoiced;
at night the two brahmins sit and reason.

353All that they argue, [the others] do not accept,
and refute it with the evidence of those same shastras.

354At night, lying down to sleep, the brahmins talk;
one says: "These two are great souls.

355Ah, brother, what we studied under our teacher
does not agree with the doctrine of these two.

356They serve Krishna and serve the sadhus without cease;
these two great men are fine scholars of all the shastras.

357They have established that the highest is the worship of Ishvara;
he who does not worship is a traitor to his master, and Yama punishes him.

358I see that in the worship of Sri Krishna no shudra-hood remains;
until now I had never heard that the shastras say so."

359Saying this, the two fell into deep sleep;
towards the end of the night a great person came and says:

360"O son of a brahmin, you do not understand in your heart:
by worshipping [Krishna] brahminhood is preserved — so the shastras say.

361Those two are the gurus of your guru,50
and you are proud, taking yourself for a brahmin.

362In the morning go and take shelter at their feet;
come what may — [your] worldly existence is at an end.51

363Worship Govinda, O living being — how long [will you wait]?
All you have done till now is mere clutter."

364These two brahmins had worshipped Krishna before;
all will see the proof of it later.

365Because of a slight [lack of] bhava, the two were born in brahmin families;
birth after birth guru and disciple — that is the essence of it.52

366Rising at dawn, the two prostrated themselves
and, with joined palms, plead at length:

367"I was born in the world as a [mere] brahmin;53
now be merciful and make me a true brahmin.

368Where else can these two sinners go?
Owning us as your own, touch our heads with your feet.

369Life will not stay in my body — have pity on me;
I am scorched by the threefold misery — give me the shade of your feet.

370Your feet are spotless and grant fearlessness;
have mercy on the lowly — who else is there in the world?

371Till now the time has passed in such false delights;
there was no longing for the two feet of Sri Krishna.

372Be merciful, Prabhu, give such instruction
as to attain these two feet — that alone remains."

373Each in his mind seized hold of these two feet;
Ramakrishna [says]: "My lord, my Prabhu is Narottama."

374Harirama says: "My Prabhu is Ramachandra;
birth after birth I serve this pair of feet."

375Saying this, they weep, calling the name of their own Prabhu;
crying "Shame, shame [on us]!" they roll on the ground.

376In the heart of each of the two compassion arose for his own;
each of the two gave his own the Hari-nama mantra in his ear.

377Receiving it, they bow down, tears pouring from their eyes:
"Have mercy: what are we two to do?"

378The two say: "Always take the name of Krishna,
so that eating or sleeping there is nothing else in your minds."

379Coming out into the courtyard, they cry "Gauranga, Gauranga!"
and, gazing at the form [of the image], both fall to the ground.

380When there is kirtana, they show the transformations of bhava;
how meekly and lowly they speak of themselves!

381Some days passed thus, as they themselves wished;
[then] the two mahashayas gave the two a command.

382The brahmins bathed and came; [the mahashayas] give their command:
seating the two, they show them mercy:

383with delight in their hearts they give the Radha-Krishna mantra;
hearing the mantra, their bodies blossom in the rapture of bhava.

384Going outside, they make the eight-limbed prostration;
[the gurus] touched their heads with their feet and laid a hand on their backs.

385They were told all the limbs of sadhana;
with joy in their hearts they read the method of remembrance.

386Rapt in bliss, they practise sadhana for the goal;
when [some time] had passed, at last they were given a command:

387"Read the books of bhakti, my sons, sitting together;
in practising sadhana you will find great happiness in your minds.

388Whatever gives rise to firm attachment to sadhana —
read all those books: in them you will find the essence."

389The two read the books composed by Sri Rupa;
reading and reading, they became very learned.

390How much shall I write of the way these two worshipped?
Such mercy, such power [of theirs] we shall see later.

391There is perfected worship accumulated before;
for that reason [such a one] is born in a high family.

392A pandita has a fear of offences;
once he takes shelter, [worship] at once reveals itself.

393Later he grows mighty — great power and strength;
all the Vaishnavas sing his virtues.

394I shall write one more word — listen:
what is written in the book is made manifest everywhere.

395He whose hope is the feet of Sri Jahnava and Virachandra,
Nityananda Dasa, tells the Prema-vilasa.

Thus ends the fourteenth vilasa of the Prema-vilasa.

Notes

  1. That is, before the image of Gauranga served at Srikhanda by Narahari Sarakara and Raghunandana; "on the right" apparently means circumambulating it clockwise (pradakshina).
  2. "basāiyā grāme", literally "settling in the village"; the reading is conjectural.
  3. That is, he had died — Narahari Sarakara Thakura, Raghunandana's uncle and guru.
  4. A variant given in the 1913 edition: "he spoke of Krishna in every detail".
  5. The Nata-mandira, the hall for singing and dancing in front of a temple.
  6. A variant given in the 1913 edition: "sitting in that place, [each] contemplates [the other] in his mind". The line is obscure.
  7. This couplet is found only in the 1913 edition; it is preceded by an illegible line of OCR.
  8. Vyasa Acharya, Srinivasa's disciple from Vishnupura (cf. ch. 13).
  9. The Thakura's words are not given in either edition; apparently he invites Vyasa to continue the debate.
  10. The second line is obscure ("ṭhākurera saha vākya mora anubhava"); the translation is conjectural.
  11. The speaker is not marked; apparently Ramachandra's reply begins here (cf. 77).
  12. "kṣāra khali", lye and oil-cake, i.e. worthless food; an image of empty learning.
  13. Charanamrita, the water that has washed the feet of the guru or of a deity.
  14. "smaraṇa-paddhati", apparently a guide to remembering the lilas through the hours of the day (cf. Rupa Gosvami's Smarana-mangala).
  15. Couplets 95–96 are found only in the 1913 edition.
  16. In the 1913 edition the first word is corrupt ("…pa-padāśraya"); perhaps "rūpa-padāśraya", "shelter at Rupa's feet". Couplets 97–99 are found only in the 1913 edition.
  17. Grahani, a severe digestive disorder (chronic diarrhoea, sprue).
  18. According to tradition, Govinda Kaviraja was a Shakta, a worshipper of the Goddess, before his conversion.
  19. Aja is Brahma, Bhava is Shiva.
  20. A variant given in the 1913 edition: "calling his son, he says: 'Go and bring a seat'" (?).
  21. That is, towards evening; the reckoning of time in this couplet is unclear.
  22. A variant given in both editions: "quickly reaching the tree at the gate, they halted".
  23. Banana trees and mango leaves are signs of a festive welcome.
  24. "adhara-śeṣa", remnants of food touched by the lips (of Srinivasa).
  25. "saṁskāra", here apparently initiation (diksha); cf. 169–171.
  26. "udara-bhaṅga", a disorder of the belly, i.e. the same grahani disease.
  27. That is, the verses Govinda Dasa composed before his conversion (when he was a Shakta), as against his later Vaishnava songs.
  28. The closing lines (bhanita) of a song on Shiva and Gauri; Govindadasa is the poetic name of Govinda Kaviraja.
  29. Literally "who has an obligation (dāya)"; the reading is conjectural.
  30. A widely known song of Govindadasa ("Bhajahũ re mana…"). The last stanza lists the nine forms of bhakti (Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23); "friendship" (sakhya) is here replaced by "sakhis", i.e. service to Radha's friends; the text is partly corrupt in both editions.
  31. Vasudeva Ghosha, an associate of Mahaprabhu and author of songs on Gauranga.
  32. Rupa Gosvami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu and Ujjvala-nilamani.
  33. A variant given in both editions: "thirty-two years".
  34. Holding a straw between the teeth is a sign of utmost humility.
  35. Here begins the account of Narottama (Thakura Mahashaya) at Kheturi.
  36. The assignment of speakers in this couplet is conjectural.
  37. The sense is unclear; the "Prabhu" here is perhaps Lokanatha Gosvami. The speeches in 228–232 are assigned by sense: the speakers are not marked.
  38. The full moon of the month of Phalguna (February–March), the day of Mahaprabhu's appearance.
  39. Vallavikanta (literally "Beloved of the cowherd women") is Krishna; images of Gauranga and of several forms of Krishna were installed at Kheturi.
  40. Ukhra, a sweet made of puffed rice with molasses.
  41. A variant given in both editions: "as if the time [of the festival at] Kshetra (Puri) had come".
  42. Panchamrita, a mixture of milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar for bathing a deity.
  43. The shimul, the silk-cotton tree with a thorny trunk; an image of hair standing on end (pulaka).
  44. Apparently Krishnananda; the subject is unclear.
  45. The sense of the second line is unclear; the translation is conjectural.
  46. The alapa, the unmetred introduction to a song, without words.
  47. Before this both editions have "sādhā sādhā" (?), perhaps a corruption of "rādhā".
  48. Purva-raga, love before the first meeting, the initial stage of love in the doctrine of rasa.
  49. That is, the evening worship of the Gauranga installed by Narottama at Kheturi.
  50. The sense of the line is apparently that Narottama and Ramachandra stand above these brahmins' own teachers.
  51. The second line is obscure: "je hau se hau mora saṁsāra gela kṣaya" (the 1999 edition has "saṁśaya", "doubt"); perhaps these are already the brahmin's words.
  52. The couplet is found only in the 1913 edition; the sense is conjectural.
  53. So the 1913 edition ("a-brāhmaṇa"), "as a non-brahmin", i.e. a brahmin by birth only; the 1999 edition has "as a brahmin".
